evidence_spans.snippet: 64-byte Page Write Mode (Partial Page Writes Allowed)
The A1 and A0 pins are device address inputs that are hardwired or left not connected for hardware compatibility with other AT24CXX devices.
WRITE PROTECT (WP): The write protect input, when connected to GND, allows normal write operations. When WP is connected high to VCC, all write operations to the memory are inhibited.
The Write Cycle Time of 5 ms only applies to the AT24C128/256 devices bearing the process letter 'B' on the package
A high-to-low transition of SDA with SCL high is a start condition which must precede any other command
A low-to-high transition of SDA with SCL high is a stop condition.
The EEPROM sends a zero during the ninth clock cycle to acknowledge that it has received each word.

After an interruption in protocol, power loss or system reset, any two-wire part can be reset by following these steps: (a) Clock up to 9 cycles, (b) look for SDA high in each cycle while SCL is high and then (c) create a start condition as SDA is high.
The device address word consists of a mandatory one, zero sequence for the first five most significant bits as shown.
The 128K/256K uses the two device address bits A1, A0 to allow as many as four devices on the same bus.
The eighth bit of the device address is the read/write operation select bit.
A write operation requires two 8-bit data word addresses following the device address word and acknowledgment.
The 128K/256K EEPROM is capable of 64-byte page writes.
Once the internally-timed write cycle has started and the EEPROM inputs are disabled, acknowledge polling can be initiated.
Read operations are initiated the same way as write operations with the exception that the read/write select bit in the device address word is set to one.
A random read requires a 'dummy' byte write sequence to load in the data word address.
Sequential reads are initiated by either a current address read or a random address read.
fSCL: 100 kHz at 1.8V, 400 kHz at 2.5V, 1 MHz at 5.0V

requires_human: Determine the correct device address bits A1 and A0 based on hardware connections.
Select appropriate timing parameters based on supply voltage (1.8V, 2.5V, or 5.0V) and device variant (standard or 'B' process).
Decide whether to use delay or acknowledge polling after write operations.
Handle write protection via WP pin if needed.
